Enables the transfer of a specific lipid molecule from one membrane to another, coupled with the simultaneous counter-transfer of a different lipid molecule in the opposite direction.

nodes.lbl: negative regulation of starch biosynthetic process

definition.val: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of starch.

A protein complex that acts as a receptor for the neuroprotective peptide humanin (HN). In humans the receptor complex is a trimer composed of CNTFR, IL6ST and IL27RA. HN binding to IL27RA and CNTFR induces oligomerization of the three subunits.

The process in which spermatids lose their mitochondrial nucleoids during spermatid development. This process involves the controlled elimination of mitochondrial DNA-protein complexes while preserving the mitochondrial membranes and and contributes to maternal mitochondrial inheritance patterns by inhibiting paternal transmission.

A protein complex that mediates the transport of lipids between membranes, in which a lipid molecule or molecules is transferred through an aqueous phase from the outer leaflet of a donor membrane to the outer leaflet of an acceptor membrane.

A process of mitochondrial translational elongation that takes place when a mitochondrial ribosome has stalled during translation, and results in freeing the ribosome from the stalled translation complex.

A cellular process which results in an increase in the size (surface area) of the plasma membrane during cell growth or osmotic stress. This can occur by lipid transfer, membrane trafficking, or eisosome disassembly.

nodes.lbl: positive regulation of plasma membrane expansion

definition.val: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of plasma membrane expansion.

nodes.lbl: negative regulation of enteroendocrine cell differentiation

definition.val: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of enteroendocrine cell differentiation.

The process in which relatively unspecialized cells acquire specialized structural and/or functional features of an intestinal enterochromaffin enteroendocrine cell. Enterochromaffin enteroendocrine cells are found in the gastrointestinal mucosa and secrete serotonin and some neurotransmitters including enkephalins and substance P.

nodes.lbl: intestinal type G enteroendocrine cell differentiation

definition.val: The process in which relatively unspecialized cells acquire specialized structural and/or functional features of an intestinal type G enteroendocrine cell. Intestinal type G enteroendocrine cells are found in the stomach and duodenum and are responsible for the secretion of gastrin and enkephalin.

nodes.lbl: intestinal type I enteroendocrine cell differentiation

definition.val: The process in which relatively unspecialized cells acquire specialized structural and/or functional features of an intestinal type I enteroendocrine cell. Intestinal type I enteroendocrine cells are found in the duodenum and jejunum and secrete cholecystokinin.

nodes.lbl: intestinal type L enteroendocrine cell differentiation

definition.val: The process in which relatively unspecialized cells acquire specialized structural and/or functional features of an intestinal type L enteroendocrine cell. Intestinal type L enteroendocrine cells are found in ileum and large intestine and secrete glucagon-like peptides.

nodes.lbl: intestinal type N enteroendocrine cell differentiation

definition.val: The process in which relatively unspecialized cells acquire specialized structural and/or functional features of an intestinal type N enteroendocrine cell. Intestinal type N enteroendocrine cells are found in the ileum and jejunum and secrete neurotensin.

nodes.lbl: intestinal type D enteroendocrine cell differentiation

definition.val: The process in which relatively unspecialized cells acquire specialized structural and/or functional features of an intestinal type D enteroendocrine cell. Intestinal type D enteroendocrine cells are found in the gastrointestinal tract and in the pancreas and secrete somatostatin.
Enables the transfer of N(6),N(6),N(6)-trimethyl-L-lysine from one side of a membrane to the other.
Enables the transfer of dimethylarginine from one side of a membrane to the other.

OBSOLETE. Binding specifically to a glycoprotein (cargo) to deliver it to a transport vesicle. Glycoprotein cargo receptors span membranes, binding simultaneously to cargo molecules and coat adaptors, to efficiently recruit the cargo molecules to nascent vesicles.

comments: The reason for obsoletion is that this term was added in error. Most vesicle cargo are glycoproteins, so classifying cargo receptors by glycoprotein substrate introduces an additional, unhelpful axis of classification. Cargo receptor activities should instead be organized by transport domain (i.e., the vesicles they connect cargo to), with substrates captured via has_input.

definition.val: Combining with phosphatidylserine and transmitting the signal from one side of the membrane to the other to initiate a change in cell activity.

A heterotetrameric cGMP phosphodiesterase complex found in the disc membranes of rod photoreceptor outer segments. It consists of two catalytic subunits, PDE6A and PDE6B, and two inhibitory gamma-subunits, PDE6G. In response to activation by transducin, the complex hydrolyzes cyclic GMP, thereby mediating the light-induced closure of cGMP-gated ion channels during rod phototransduction.
Binding to a sodium ion to prevent it from interacting with other partners or to inhibit its localization to the area of the cell or complex where it is active.

OBSOLETE. The directed movement of tyramine into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Tyramine is a monoamine neurotransmitter occurring predominantly in invertebrates.

comments: The reason for obsoletion is that this is an unnecessary grouping term and annotations should be made to more mechanism/location specific terms.

definition.val: The directed movement of octopamine into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Octopamine is a monoamine neurotransmitter occurring predominantly in invertebrates.
The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of nickel-pincer nucleotide (NPN) cofactor, also known as nickel pyridinium-3,5-bisthiocarboxylic acid mononucleotide.

nodes.lbl: negative regulation of ER to Golgi vesicle-mediated transport

definition.val: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of ER to Golgi vesicle-mediated transport.
Catalysis of the reaction: L-threonyl-[protein] + FAD = FMN-L-threonyl-[protein] + AMP + H+.

The process by which central nervous system glial and associated cells assemble and stabilize a dense, organized glial border at the site of injury. This involves proliferation and reorganization of reactive astrocytes and NG2 glia (oligodendrocyte precursor cells), deposition of extracellular matrix components, and formation of a barrier that modulates inflammation and regeneration.

comments: Distinct from connective tissue replacement involved in inflammatory response wound healing (GO:0002248) as CNS glial scars differ in cellular origin and molecular composition.

definition.val: Any process that reduces the pH of the melanosomal lumen, corresponding to an increase in hydrogen ion concentration.
Any process that increases the pH of the melanosomal lumen, corresponding to a decrease in hydrogen ion concentration.

The outermost lipid bilayer surrounding complex plastids in organisms that acquired their plastids through secondary endosymbiosis. This membrane is derived from the host cell's endomembrane system and is continuous with the rough endoplasmic reticulum and the outer nuclear envelope. In some species, the cytoplasmic face may be studded with ribosomes.

The lipid bilayer that forms the second outermost membrane of complex plastids in organisms that acquired their plastids through secondary endosymbiosis. The periplastidial membrane is evolutionarily derived from the plasma membrane of the engulfed algal endosymbiont and together with the outer envelope membrane of the plastid defines the periplastidial compartment.

A membrane-associated protein complex found in archaea that consists of sugar binding proteins assembled via a type IV pilin-like assembly system. The complex is located at the cell surface and functions in sugar uptake by facilitating the interaction between solute binding proteins and ABC transporters. The complex forms high molecular mass structures (400-600 kDa) that are integrated within or closely associated with the S-layer.

Binding to a lipid and delivering it to an acceptor protein, including enzymes, nuclear receptors, and other lipid-binding proteins. The lipid may be presented while bound to the chaperone for enzymatic modification or signaling, or fully transferred to the acceptor protein.
Catalysis of the reaction: biliverdin IXalpha + 2 reduced ferredoxin + 4 H+ = (3Z)-phycoerythrobilin + 2 oxidized ferredoxin.
Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of GCN2-mediated signaling.
OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the reaction: ATP + N6-methyladenosine = ADP + H+ + N6-methyl-AMP.

comments: The reason for obsoletion is that this term was added in error.

definition.val: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the reaction: ATP + N6,N6-dimethyladenosine = ADP + H+ + N6,N6-dimethyl-AMP.

comments: The reason for obsoletion is that this term was added in error.

definition.val: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the reaction: ATP + N6-isopentenyladenosine = ADP + H+ + N6-isopentenyl-AMP.

comments: The reason for obsoletion is that this term was added in error.

definition.val: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the reaction: H2O + H+ + N6,N6-dimethyl-AMP = IMP + dimethylamine.

comments: The reason for obsoletion is that this term was added in error.

definition.val: OBSOLETE. Catalysis of the reaction: H2O + H+ + N6-isopentenyl-AMP = IMP + dimethylallylamine.

comments: The reason for obsoletion is that this term was added in error.

definition.val: An organelle membrane contact site between the mitochondrial outer membrane and the lysosomal membrane.
An organelle membrane contact site between the endoplasmic reticulum membrane and the lysosomal membrane.

A protein complex that contains one or more nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat (NLR) proteins and functions as an intracellular innate immune receptor. Upon activation by pathogen effectors or danger signals, the complex oligomerizes with adaptor and effector proteins to trigger downstream immune responses including programmed cell death.
Catalysis of the reaction: S-adenosyl-L-methionine + adenosine(37) in tRNA(Val) = S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine + N(6)-methyladenosine(37) in tRNA(Val) + H+.
Any process that reduces the pH of the intestinal lumen, corresponding to an increase in hydrogen ion concentration.
Any process that reduces the pH of an extracellular fluid of a multicellular organism, corresponding to an increase in hydrogen ion concentration.

synonyms.val: multicellular organismal-level extracellular fluid pH reduction

nodes.lbl: copper ion import into Golgi lumen

definition.val: The directed import of copper cation from the cytosol across the Golgi membrane into the Golgi lumen.

synonyms.val: copper ion import across Golgi membrane
copper ion import into Golgi apparatus
copper ion import into the Golgi
cytosol to Golgi apparatus copper transport

definition.val: The import of proteins from the cytosol to their final destination in the mitochondria.

nodes.lbl: alpha helical protein insertion into mitochondrial outer membrane

definition.val: The import of alpha helical and tail-anchored proteins from the cytosol and their insertion into the mitochondrial outer membrane.

comments: In yeast, the insertase is the mitochondrial import (MIM) complex, composed of Mim1 and Mim2. In higher eukaryotes, the functional counterpart MTCH performs a similar role despite lacking sequence and structural homology, reflecting convergent evolution.

nodes.lbl: TOM-TIM23-SORT-mediated protein insertion into the mitochondrial inner membrane

definition.val: The import of proteins from the cytosol across the outer mitochondrial membrane and laterally inserted into the inner membrane. Typically acting on single-pass transmembrane proteins with an N-terminal targeting sequence and an internal hydrophobic stop-transfer sequence which targets them for lateral insertion.

comments: Some proteins utilize this pathway but can be further processed and released from the inner membrane into the IMS.

nodes.lbl: TOM-TIM22-mediated mitochondrial inner membrane protein insertion

definition.val: The import of multipass-membrane proteins from the cytosol and their insertion into the mitochondrial inner membrane, supported by tiny-tim chaperones.
A membrane-membrane adaptor activity that provides the first point of contact and physically bridges the vesicle membrane and its target membrane prior to vesicle docking and fusion.

nodes.lbl: beta barrel protein insertion into mitochondrial outer membrane

definition.val: The import of beta barrel proteins from the cytosol and their insertion into the mitochondrial outer membrane.
An adaptor activity that brings together two actin filaments, enabling the bundling or networking of actin filaments (F-actin).
The binding activity of a molecule that brings together the peroxisome membrane and the chloroplast membrane, establishing the localization of the peroxisome close to the chloroplast.

The binding activity of a molecule that brings together an endoplasmic reticulum membrane and a vacuole membrane either via membrane lipid binding or by interacting with a membrane protein, to establish or maintain membrane contact sites.

The binding activity of a molecule that brings together the contractile vacuolar membrane and the plasma membrane, either via membrane lipid binding or by interacting with a membrane protein, to establish or maintain the localization of the contractile vacuole at a specific plasma membrane discharge site.
Catalysis of the reaction: 2 Fe2+ + NADP+ + H+ = 2 Fe3+ + NADPH.
The selective degradation of ferritin to release iron by macroautophagy.

A conserved, hetero-oligomeric (often tetrameric) cycling ER-Golgi protein complex that selectively recruits secretory cargo, especially GPI-anchored proteins, into COPII vesicles and helps maintain early secretory pathway organization. A functional p24 complex typically contains one member of each subfamily of p24 proteins, alpha, beta, gamma and delta.
A process by which an organism causes inflammatory response in another organism via the action of a venom.

synonyms.val: envenomation resulting in positive regulation of inflammatory response in another organism

definition.val: Combining with a double-stranded RNA and transmitting the signal to initiate an innate immune response.

Combining with a left-handed Z-RNA and transmitting the signal to initiate an innate immune response. Z-RNA is a left-handed double-helical conformation of RNA in which the phosphate backbone zigzags.

A glycoprotein biosynthetic process in which a single N-acetylglucosamine is covalently linked via a beta-glycosidic bond to the oxygen atom of a serine or threonine side chain in a protein, resulting in the formation of a protein O-linked glycan. The sugar is not elongated into a larger oligosaccharide chain.
A venom-mediated activation of inflammatory response that triggers leucocyte infiltration in another organism.

synonyms.val: envenomation resulting in positive regulation of leukocyte migration involved in inflammatory response in another organism

definition.val: A venom-mediated activation of inflammatory response that triggers release of an inflammatory mediator in another organism. Inflammatory mediators include cytokines or interleukins.

synonyms.val: envenomation resulting in positive regulation of production of molecular mediator involved in inflammatory response in another organism
